question: Can a prompt that requires a causal SAE check improve an editor's patch over the existing no-fit and native baselines?
treatment: Use the shared --sae-guided policy, fit on balanced public examples at a decision position, suppress a learned feature, compare target and preservation margins, then edit and verify.
source_comparisons: Previously scored seed-2 no-fit, 6 turns / 2048 output limit
Previously scored native IWIBench seed-2, 12 turns / 4096 output limit
Previously scored first instructed SAE workflow, 6 turns / 2048 output limit
transfer: Replay the new, no-fit, and native seed-2 patches on the first two pristine-eligible development seeds from 12 through 20 in increasing order. Select on pristine admission only. No new editing on those seeds and no hidden results shown to the editor.
endpoints: actual use of fitting and causal intervention
interpretation: This is development of the editing policy after inspecting the earlier seed-2 outcomes. Prespecified transfer checks evaluate the same frozen patch on new seeds of the same family. The different run budgets and single editor sample preclude inferring a standalone causal effect of the SAE.
failure: Keep the first trajectory and any provider stop or failure. Do not reroll using hidden outcomes.
